digest_markdown:
• A GitHub Actions supply chain attack targets the trust chain inside CI/CD, compromising workflows, reusable actions, dependencies, or secrets to influence what gets built, signed, published, or deployed. [1]

• SHA pinning, which involves pinning to a specific commit SHA, has been shown to be vulnerable to bypass attacks, as demonstrated by the Trivy attackers who exploited a gap in operational trust and developer behavior. [2]

• A malicious workflow component has propagated into tens of thousands of repositories, silently exfiltrating CI/CD secrets during pipeline execution, and organizations that reference the compromised workflow component may have executed attacker-controlled code. [3]

• The attack chain involves an upstream compromise, automatic propagation, execution in a privileged context, and secret harvesting, with the malicious payload running inside the GitHub runner process and scraping runner process memory for secret material. [3]

• The attack highlights the need for organizations to assume that any repository referencing the compromised workflow component may have executed attacker-controlled code and to verify their current posture and act on the guidance provided. [3]
